fieldParsing.notes: Full frontmatter table documented: name, description, when_to_use, argument-hint, arguments, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, allowed-tools, disallowed-tools, model, effort, context, agent, background, hooks, paths, shell, metadata, license, compatibility. Boolean fields accept yes/no/on/off/1/0 since v2.1.218 (true/false only before). Unexpected keys reject only via claude.ai/Skills-API upload paths, not Claude Code itself.

discoveryLocations.notes: Personal ~/.claude/skills/, project .claude/skills/ (root + parent dirs up to repo root), nested subdirectory skills load lazily on first file touch, --add-dir grants auto-loaded skills, plugin skills namespaced plugin:skill. Precedence: enterprise > personal > project > bundled. Live change detection picks up edits without restart; new top-level dirs need a restart.

invocationBehavior.notes: disable-model-invocation (default false) blocks auto-invoke, subagent preload, and (v2.1.196+) scheduled-task firing. user-invocable (default true) controls /-menu visibility only. The two are independent, not mutually exclusive when combined to fully lock a skill. /name always works regardless of disable-model-invocation.

contextLoading.notes: Description always resident; full body loads only on invocation (progressive disclosure). context: fork runs the skill in a forked subagent (agent: picks type, background: default true). Re-invocation with identical rendered content adds a short note instead of duplicating full content (v2.1.202+); dynamic context injection reruns the command each time.

toolSemantics.notes: allowed-tools pre-approves tools for the invoking turn only (grant clears on next message) -- an approval grant, not a persistent restriction. disallowed-tools removes tools from the pool while active, also turn-scoped. Neither field durably enforces a sidecar's declared-non-empty tools list as an exclusive, session-wide allowlist without additional permissions.deny configuration.

pathControls.notes: Two parallel, differently-syntaxed mechanisms: permission rules (Read()/Edit() allow/deny, //abs vs /project-relative) are prompt-gated, not OS-enforced; sandbox.filesystem.allowRead/denyRead/allowWrite/denyWrite (/, ~/, ./ prefixes) are OS-enforced but only inside the opt-in Bash sandbox. An adapter must configure both paths separately -- neither alone restricts all file access vectors.

sandboxControls.notes: Real OS-level sandbox (macOS Seatbelt; Linux/WSL2 bubblewrap+socat, optional seccomp). Off by default (sandbox.enabled). Escape hatch: a command that fails sandboxed may retry via dangerouslyDisableSandbox, falling to the regular permission flow rather than hard-failing, unless allowUnsandboxedCommands:false (Strict sandbox mode) is explicitly set. sandbox.failIfUnavailable hard-fails on missing dependencies instead of silently running unsandboxed.

networkControls.notes: Bash-sandbox network isolation (network.allowedDomains/deniedDomains, strictAllowlist, allowManagedDomainsOnly) is a separate mechanism from WebFetch's own permission-rule domain approval -- explicitly documented as sandboxed-commands-only; in-process tools like WebFetch follow permission rules instead. A single 'block network' requirement needs both configured; configuring only one leaves the other tool category uncovered.

mcpLifecycle.notes: disabledMcpServers/enabledMcpServers control whether a server connects at all, distinct from a permission-rule deny on one mcp__server__tool -- disabling a tool is not the same as preventing its server from loading. Remote servers may show a cached tool list from a prior session and connect lazily on first tool call (v2.1.221+, MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE=0 forces eager connect); list_changed notifications refresh capabilities without reconnect.

pluginSubagentLimitations.notes: A subagent's tools: field is narrowed by two hidden filters beyond what's declared: a fixed list removed from every subagent, and a further reduction for background-mode subagents (the default) that strips most built-ins except a named allowlist. The same tools: declaration therefore resolves to a different effective set in foreground vs. background -- reading tools: alone understates the restriction.
